data.long_meaning: Prithvija is a unisex name of Sanskrit origin, meaning 'Queen of the Earth'. data.cultural_impact: The name Prithvija symbolizes a deep connection and reverence for the earth and its nurturing qualities. In many Hindu cultures, the land is considered sacred and blesses the people with abundant resources. Thus, the name Prithvija represents the motherly and caring nature of the earth and the importance of preserving and treasuring it.
data.spiritual_significance: In Hinduism, the earth is considered one of the five primary elements, which form the foundation of life. Prithvija can be seen as a reflection of the divine feminine aspect, symbolizing the nourishing, fertile energy of creation. Her spiritual significance stems from her role in supporting life, providing sustenance, and fostering growth. Thus, the name Prithvija serves as a reminder of our interconnectedness with the natural world and the importance of respecting and honoring it.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Prithvija: Earth-victory. Symbolizing the triumph over earthly desires, anchoring oneself to the stable foundation of the earth while striving for spiritual growth.

vedic_reference.note: Not found in Vedas or Upanishads

historical_references.reference: The name Prithvija is derived from the Sanskrit word Prithvi meaning 'earth'. It is believed that the name was used to signify the ruler of the earth or the king of the world. Prithvija was also a name of the ancient Indian god of the earth, Lord Prithvi. In Hindu mythology, Lord Prithvi is considered the father of all living beings and the sustainer of the universe.
historical_references.context: Hindu mythology and ancient Indian history

historical_references.reference: Another reference to Prithvija can be found in the Hindu epic Mahabharata. In this text, there is a mention of a king named Prithvijasena, who ruled over the entire earth. He was a just and powerful ruler who maintained peace and prosperity in his kingdom. Prithvijasena is considered an incarnation of Lord Vishnu and is revered in Hindu tradition as a symbol of righteous rule and devotion to the welfare of his people.
historical_references.context: Hindu epics and ancient Indian history
